SIAS to launch 'Invest Singapore' to improve financial literacy and confidence for new generation of investors
article:
David Gerald is calling for more ways to promote financial literacy among the younger generation, so that they will be savvy and active investors familiar with the local stock market as they grow up.

"Singapore has an extensive system of government support for families raising children. Based on estimates, a Singaporean child may receive close to $70,000 in support by age 17, depending on family circumstances and eligibility," says the founder, president and CEO of the Securities Investors Association (Singapore), at the Investors' Choice Awards 2026 event on Oct 21.

"What if parents were to use a portion of these funds to do something more to help secure their children’s financial future?" asks Gerald.

"One possibility is to encourage parents, where the relevant scheme permits, to use a portion of the financial support they receive to make voluntary top-ups to their children’s CPF accounts, preferably the Special Account which pays a guaranteed 4% compound interest per annum," he suggests.

Upon unleashing the power of compounding, the child may have almost $20,000 when he or she reaches adulthood at 21, "certainly a useful headstart in accumulating retirement savings," says Gerald.

Parents may perhaps want to set aside a small sum regularly in simple, diversified and low-cost and less risky investments such as exchange-traded funds, ETF, and tracking the Straits Times Index.

See also: Finance leaders spar over AI bubble after warning by Griffin

Once the child turns 18 and is eligible to open his or her own Central Depository Account or CDP account, the investment can be transferred from the parents’ CDP to the child, says Gerald.

He believes that by doing so, a habit can be cultivated.

"Imagine a child who grows up knowing he or she owns a small investment in some of Singapore’s leading companies. As the child grows older, parents can explain what these companies do, why their share prices fluctuate, how dividends work, and why investing requires patience.

See also: Lenovo seeking US$2 bil loan to refinance debt at lower cost — Bloomberg

"The child begins to understand that investing is not simply about buying something today to sell tomorrow at a higher price. They learn that it is about ownership, discipline, risk, and long-term wealth creation," says Gerald.

He believes that if young Singaporeans can become familiar with saving and investing from an early age, they will be financially literate and also financially confident and empowered.

"And that, I would suggest, is one of the best investments we can make in Singapore’s future. We will certainly advance this idea when we launch and implement the 'Invest Singapore' programme for families," says Gerald.

At the event on Oct 21, the SIAS honoured 45 award recipients across seven categories at this year's Investors’ Choice Awards 2026, recognising these Singapore-listed companies for excellence in corporate governance, sustainability, transparency and shareholder communications.

Held as part of SIAS' Corporate Governance Week 2026, themed “Strengthening Investor Trust: Board Accountability Across Risk, Capital and Disclosure”, the awards underscore the importance of sound corporate governance, transparent disclosures and meaningful shareholder engagement in supporting sustainable, long-term value creation.

Companies given the Singapore Corporate Governance Award are Jardine Matheson Southeast Asia, Sats, Qaf, Vicom, Hafary Holdings, Sing Holdings, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust, Keppel and Singapore Exchange.

Companies given the Corporate Sustainability Award are City Developments, Singapore Land Group, Far East Orchard, OKP Holdings, Taka Jewellery Holdings, Engro Corporation, Netlink NBN Trust and Keppel Infrastructure Trust.

For the Shareholder Communications Excellence Award, the winners are United Overseas Bank, ComfortDelGro Corp, Singapore Post, Civmec, Qian Hu Corp, The Trendlines Group, Starhill Global REIT and CDL Hospitality Trusts.

Singapore Airlines, Thai Beverage, Banyan Tree Holdings, Sing Investments & Finance, GP Industries, JB Foods, Singapore Shipping Corp, CapitaLand India Trust won for the Most Transparent Company Award.

Three company head honchos were given the Outstanding CEO Award. They are Inderbethal Singh Thakral of Thakral Corp, Loh Boon Chye of Singapore Exchange and Loh Chin Hua of Keppel. Tiger Brokers and Phillip Securities were given the Best Retail Broker award.

"The Investors’ Choice Awards celebrate companies and individuals who have demonstrated a strong commitment to good governance, transparency and the interests of shareholders. These are important qualities that help build confidence in our capital markets," says Gerald.

"By recognising their achievements, we hope to encourage more companies to adopt good governance practices, engage meaningfully with investors and uphold high standards of accountability. We also acknowledge the important contributions of corporate leaders, financial intermediaries and journalists in supporting a well-informed and engaged investing community," he adds.

This year's ICA recognised recipients across seven categories: the Singapore Corporate Governance Award, Singapore Corporate Sustainability Award, Shareholder Communications Excellence Award, Most Transparent Company Award, Investors’ Choice Outstanding CEO Award, Best Retail Broker Award and Financial Journalist Award.

The corporate awards recognise listed companies across different market capitalisation segments, as well as REITs and business trusts, for their achievements in corporate governance, sustainability, transparency and shareholder communications. The individual and industry awards honour corporate leaders, financial intermediaries and journalists whose contributions support investor education, responsible corporate practices and greater market transparency.

Together, these awards recognise the wider ecosystem of stakeholders who play an important role in strengthening investor confidence and fostering a culture of accountability across Singapore's capital markets.

title: Nasdaq 100 climbs as SpaceX results fuel AI trade
article:
(Oct 21): A blockbuster earnings report from SpaceX spurred a rally in technology stocks, easing concerns over whether a global investment spree in artificial intelligence (AI) can prove sustainable.

The 12% surge in the satellite, rocket and AI conglomerate was also fuelled by Elon Musk’s remarks endorsing the prospect of a merger with Tesla Inc. The electric-car maker and Meta Platforms Inc will report results later on Wednesday. Super Micro Computer Inc jumped on solid preliminary figures. The Nasdaq 100 outperformed major benchmarks as chipmakers climbed.

“So, does this signal that the worst is over when it comes to the selloff across tech, and in particular chip stocks, seen since the beginning of this month? Maybe,” said David Morrison at Trade Nation. “Certainly, there has been yet another impressive start to the earnings season.”

Investors’ anxiety over the durability of the AI boom had surged in recent weeks amid fears that the substantial upfront capital spending the technology needs will take longer than expected to translate into profits and productivity gains.

Billionaire Ken Griffin said investors are “almost certainly” in the midst of an AI bubble as many companies are still grappling with just how much they’ll spend on the technology and how it will transform the economy.

See also: Abbott to spin off baby formula business

BlackRock Inc chief executive officer Larry Fink warned that delays in building data centres could raise computing costs and threaten economic growth as demand for AI accelerates.

“If we don’t build out these data centres, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now,” Fink said in an interview on Bloomberg Television on Wednesday, on the sidelines of the Berlin Global Dialogue event. “And the faster we can build out more data centres, the more compute we have, the faster we can bring down the cost.”

See also: US chip stocks post longest losing streak since 2008

Elsewhere, the yield on benchmark French debt hit 5% for the first time since 2002 as elevated energy prices exacerbated concern over the country’s fiscal outlook.

Oil was little changed with attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continuing to menace supplies, though flows through the waterway remain robust. Iran said the US must lift its naval blockade and show it’s serious about ending the war diplomatically, as a deadlock over talks and growing threats from both sides fuel fears of a return to outright conflict.

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The S&P 500 was little changed as of 10.08am New York time
• The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was little changed
• The euro was little changed at US$1.1226
• The British pound was little changed at US$1.3383
• The Japanese yen was little changed at 158.07 per dollar

title: Super Micro jumps after positive preliminary results top estimates
article:
(Oct 21): Shares of Super Micro Computer Inc jumped after the company reported preliminary quarterly results that topped analysts’ estimates.

The server maker said sales will be US$18.5 billion to US$19.5 billion in the quarter that ended Sept 30. Analysts, on average, estimated US$15 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Gross margins will be in the range of 12% to 12.5%, Super Micro said on Tuesday in a statement.

The company has been benefitting from surging demand for gear to train and run artificial intelligence (AI) tasks. Super Micro’s servers are fitted with the Nvidia Corp chips that have become the preferred components for the vast majority of AI data centres. The company also has been in the limelight for a probe that accused a co-founder and two others of illegally diverting billions of dollars’ worth of servers to China in violation of US law. The firm hasn’t been charged in the case and an independent probe concluded Super Micro’s senior management had no knowledge of the purported scheme.

The shares jumped as much as 15% to US$37.45 after markets opened in New York on Wednesday, their biggest intraday gain in over two months.

The company said it would review the results during a conference call scheduled for Nov 3. The company gave no reason for announcing the earnings in advance of the scheduled date for the report.

title: Former Hungarian central bank governor detained, says report
article:
(Oct 21): Former Hungarian central bank governor Gyorgy Matolcsy was detained on Wednesday on suspicion of fraud as as the crackdown on alleged corruption of the previous ruling elite continues.

Matolcsy ran the institution for 12 years until 2025 and was a close associate of the previous prime minister, Viktor Orban, before their falling out. Under his leadership, the central bank became mired in scandals involving diversion of public money and self-enrichment by members of his family.

Hungary’s current prime minister, Peter Magyar, confirmed the decision in a Facebook post on Wednesday. Matolcsy’s lawyer, Pal Batki, told Telex website, which was first to report the detention, that his client was “suspected of fraud and document falsification alleged to have caused material financial losses.”

Matolcsy’s lawyer submitted a complaint saying the detention was unwarranted, Telex said.

The former central banker is the most emblematic of the people so far detained by Hungarian authorities probing cases of graft committed during Orban’s rule, which became increasingly authoritarian before he was ousted in a landslide in April. It follows detention of two former ministers as part of separate corruption probes.

Allegations against Matolcsy have centred on a refurbishment of the bank’s headquarters and a series of real estate investments by foundations that were endowed by the bank. Matolcsy has responded to the allegations in a series of videos posted to social media in which he denied any wrongdoing.

See also: Carrefour cuts profit forecast after riots, looting in France

“I keep hearing that the money disappeared,” he said in a post earlier this month. “The truth, by contrast, is we know exactly where it is: most of it is in real estate in 12 cities in Central Europe.”

The central bank in Budapest had no immediate comment on Wednesday. Matolcsy’s successor as governor, Mihaly Varga, who is also a former Orban minister, has been cooperating with the investigations into the bank’s previous management, including by making thousands of pages of documents available for the probes.

At the same time, Magyar has exempted Varga from his purge of Orban-era appointees to respect central bank independence.

See also: VW’s Scania hastens China e-truck push as drivers abandon diesel

Prosecutors, who conducted searches at various premises relating to the case early on Wednesday, promised an update for later in the day. Under Hungarian criminal law, the authorities have three days before moving to a formal arrest, which can then be extended almost indefinitely if required by a judge.

Matolcsy, who served as economy minister before Orban appointed him to the central bank in 2013, was one of the authors of Orban’s “unorthodox” economic policies. Those included measures like nationalising private pension funds rather than seeking aid from the International Monetary Fund.

But while Orban once described Matolcsy as his “right hand” man, relations between the two became strained as details about the scale of the alleged self-dealing leaked to the media, with stories about gilded toilet brushes in the bank’s headquarters jostling for space alongside news of his son’s supercars.

Orban’s government and the central bank also became locked in a years-long policy dispute, with Matolcsy urging greater fiscal restraint and the cabinet backing stimulus programmes and calling for more aggressive reductions to then highest borrowing costs in the European Union.

title: MAS to support SIAS in developing IPO guides that distil key information from public offer documents
article:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will support the Securities Investors Association (Singapore) or SIAS develop IPO guides, says Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat, who is also MAS's deputy chairman. Chee made the announcement at SIAS’ Investors Choice Awards on Oct 21.

The guides will distil key information from public offer documents, help investors identify key metrics and highlight matters that warrant a closer look. The guides will not recommend whether an IPO is a good or bad investment, Chee says.

“The objective is to help investors ask the right questions and make more informed decisions,” he stresses.

“Investor empowerment should not end when a company lists,” he adds.

In addition, MAS is reviewing its regulations to see if there are ways to support more independent research of IPOs.

“An IPO marks the beginning of a company’s relationship with the wider investment community,” says Chee. “Investors need continued access to meaningful information and opportunities for constructive engagement with the companies they invest in.”

See also: JP Morgan Singapore & Asia Equity Income Fund surpasses $1 bil AUM in eight months

At the dinner, Chee spotlighted the Equity Market Development Programme’s (EQDP) progress. The first two phases of the EQDP have laid a “strong foundation”, he says.

This year, the equities market saw average daily volumes (ADV) exceeding over $2 billion, 40% higher y-o-y, he notes.

See also: MAS places $1.45 bil with five asset managers; reviewing proposals for a fourth batch of asset managers

The market is also seeing broader participation beyond its largest stocks. Turnover for the Next50 constituents also increased by 93% from 2025. A growing number of small- and mid-cap stocks are also now able to absorb institutional flows. SGX also welcomed 10 new listings this year, raising $1.4 billion.

“Through the EQDP, our appointed fund managers have been crowding in more capital into Singapore equities,” he says. “What this means in practice is that for every dollar of public funds invested through EQDP, we are seeing more than a dollar of private capital come alongside it – a crowd-in ratio of more than 1:1 to date.”

On the proposal to consolidate listing review functions under SGX Regco first announced last October, Chee says MAS and the regulator will be issuing their consultation responses “soon” and are targeting to effect the change in January 2027.
